questions.question: Why is String immutable in Java?
explanations: Correct. Immutability provides security (for URLs, classes, etc.), enables the string pool, and makes Strings thread-safe.
No. Immutability can consume more memory due to the creation of temporary objects.
No. Speed is not the main reason for immutability.
No. There are important technical reasons for immutability.

questions.question: What is String.intern()?
options: Adds the String to the pool and returns the pool reference
Creates a copy of the String
explanations: Correct. intern() adds the String to the string pool (if it does not exist) and returns the pool reference.
No. It does not remove the String; it adds it to the pool.
No. It does not create a copy; it returns the existing reference or the new one in the pool.
No. It is unrelated to uppercase; it is for pool handling.

questions.question: How do you compare the content of two Strings?
explanations: Correct. equals() compares the content of the Strings. The == operator compares memory references.
No. == compares whether they are the same object in memory, not the content.
No. There is no comparar() method in String.
No. There is no match() method to compare content.

questions.question: How does substring() work in modern Java?
options: Creates a new String without copying the original array (JDK 7+ optimization)
Returns a view of the String
explanations: Correct. Since JDK 7u6, substring() creates a new String that shares the character array; it is more efficient.
No. Since JDK 7+ it does not copy the full array.
No. Strings are immutable; it cannot modify the original.
No. It does not return a view; it returns a new independent String.

questions.question: What is a TextBlock in Java?
explanations: Correct. TextBlock is a Java 15+ feature that allows writing multi-line strings using triple double quotes """.
No. It is not a block of code; it is a way to declare multi-line strings.
No. It is not a collection; it is a type of String.
No. It is not a variable; it is a form of String literal.
